title: 1987 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Consider the sequence of numbers defined recursively by \(t_1=1\) and for \(n\gt1\) by \(t_n=1+t_{\frac{n}{2}}\) when \(n\) is even and by \(t_n=\frac{1}{t_{n-1}}\) when \(n\) is odd. Given that \(t_n=\frac{19}{87},\) the sum of the digits of \(n\) is

solutions.text:
Let \(N(r)\) be the index at which the value \(r\) occurs. Reversing the recursion gives \(N(r)=2N(r-1)\) for \(r\gt1,\) and \(N(r)=N(\frac{1}{r})+1\) for \(0\lt r\lt1.\)

Starting with \(N(1)=1,\) repeated use gives \(N(2)=2,\) \(N(\frac{1}{2})=3,\) \(N(\frac{3}{2})=6,\) and \(N(\frac{2}{3})=7.\) Continuing gives \(N(\frac{5}{3})=14,\) \(N(\frac{8}{3})=28,\) \(N(\frac{3}{8})=29,\) and \(N(\frac{11}{8})=58.\)

Next, \(N(\frac{8}{11})=59,\) \(N(\frac{19}{11})=118,\) \(N(\frac{11}{19})=119,\) \(N(\frac{30}{19})=238,\) \(N(\frac{49}{19})=476,\) and \(N(\frac{68}{19})=952.\) Finally, \(N(\frac{87}{19})=1904\) and \(N(\frac{19}{87})=1905.\) Thus \(n=1905,\) whose digit sum is \(1+9+0+5=15.\)

Therefore the correct answer is A.
hints: Values greater than \(1\) come from even indices; values between \(0\) and \(1\) come from odd indices
Reverse the recursion by subtracting \(1\) from values above \(1\) and taking reciprocals of values below \(1\)
